Zamanla boylam tayini, Dünya’nın kendi e.en: Finding longitude from time rests on the fixed relationship between time and the Earth's rotation about its axis. When the time at which a celestial body crosses the local meridian is compared with the time of the same event at the Greenwich meridian, the angular difference between the two meridians gives the longitude directly. This method shows clearly why time plays a central role in celestial navigation.

Zamanla boylam yöntemi teorik olarak net.en: Finding longitude from time is clear in theory; in practice, however, chronometer error, a wrongly noted time of observation and errors in the corrected altitude act directly on the longitude obtained. So although the method is a reliable check in the open sea, on its own it does not give enough safety for navigation in confined waters.

Dünya 24 saatte 360° döndüğü için zaman.en: Since the Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours, the time difference directly corresponds to the longitude difference. This constant ratio makes it possible to find longitude by comparing chronometer time to local time.

Greenwich meridyeni ve gözlemcinin yerel.en: The Greenwich meridian and the observer's local meridian are considered together. Greenwich time is read from the chronometer.
